## Research Philosophy

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal" .philosophy-section}
My research integrates experimental methods with rigorous field studies to understand human decision-making in economic contexts. I believe that bridging controlled laboratory environments with real-world observations provides the most comprehensive insights into economic behavior.

By combining lab-experimental methods with large-scale field experiments, I seek to address both fundamental theoretical questions and practical policy challenges. This dual approach allows me to test economic theories with high internal validity while ensuring that findings have external validity and real-world applicability.
:::

## Research Themes

::: {.grid}

::: {.g-col-4 .theme}
::: {.card}
### 📈 Experimental Economics

Developing and applying experimental methods to test economic theories and understand behavioral patterns in controlled settings.

- Laboratory experiments
- Field experiments
- Online experiments
- Methodological innovations
:::
:::

::: {.g-col-4 .theme}
::: {.card}
### 🏢 Labor Economics

Investigating incentives, motivations, and structural factors that shape labor market outcomes and workplace behavior.

- Performance appraisals
- Affirmative action
- Gender and leadership
- Procedural preferences
:::
:::

::: {.g-col-4 .theme}
::: {.card}
### ❤️ Charitable Giving

Examining the psychological, social, and economic factors that influence philanthropic behavior and charitable donations.

- Religious norms in giving
- High-net-worth donor behavior
- Substitution between charities
- Household bargaining over giving
:::
:::

:::

## Current Projects

::: {.grid}

::: {.g-col-12 .project}
::: {.card}
### Narratives to Sustainable Agriculture: Evidence from Madagascar's Vanilla Farmers

::: {.badges}
[Funded by Volkswagen Foundation]{.badge .bg-primary}
[2023-2026]{.badge .bg-info}
[With Marcela Ibanez and Viviana Uruena]{.badge .bg-secondary}
:::

This project examines how narratives can influence sustainable farming practices among vanilla farmers in Madagascar. Through a series of field experiments, we test the effectiveness of different messaging strategies in promoting environmentally sustainable agricultural methods.

::: {.completion}
**Completion: 40%**
:::
:::
:::

::: {.g-col-6 .project}
::: {.card}
### Substitution between Charities

::: {.badges}
[With David Reinstein (Maastricht)]{.badge .bg-secondary}
:::

Evidence from several experiments on how people substitute between charities and whether multiple charitable appeals create crowding in or crowding out of charitable contributions.

::: {.completion}
**Completion: 75%**
:::
:::
:::

::: {.g-col-6 .project}
::: {.card}
### Behavioral Insights into Pension Savings

::: {.badges}
[With Marcela Ibanez and Sebastian Schneider]{.badge .bg-secondary}
:::

Surveys and lab-in-the-field experiments in Bogota, Colombia, exploring financial decision-making, well-being, and cognitive ability across 1200 subjects. 600 participants also completed experiments on higher-order risk preferences.

::: {.completion}
**Completion: 60%**
:::
:::
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .project}
::: {.card}
### Household Bargaining over Prosocial Decisions: Evidence from Egypt

::: {.badges}
[With Marcela Ibanez and Ghida Karbala]{.badge .bg-secondary}
:::

Representative sample of Cairo population of married women. 600 observations of household survey data and bargaining experiments over charitable donations.

::: {.completion}
**Completion: 85%**
:::
:::
:::

:::

Field experiments in Morocco examining religious norms in charitable giving.
